A 20 second cinematic race thriller, one continuous generation of seven shots, continuing straight on from the pit stop of the Port Aurelia Night Race (same night, same people, same grade). Vertical 9:16, ultra-real, ARRI Alexa 35 look, Kodak 500T grain, rich night blacks, cool floodlight and warm sodium at the track. Faces, wardrobe, the green PushOwl Racing car no. 7 and every logo exactly as in the references. BRANDS: the only logos anywhere are the fictional ones on the supplied brand boards (Meridian Series, Port Aurelia Night Race, PushOwl Racing, KALOR, GRAVIK, HALDEN, VOLTIQ, ZENTEL, HAULIX, Ember Racing, Altair Racing, Burnt Rubber Candle Co.); every other sign or screen is blank. Phone and laptop screens always face away from camera. No on-screen text, captions or subtitles.
FRAMING: from 3 s to 11 s every shot keeps its subject and all action inside the middle half of the frame height (the picture will be cropped to a wide band).
SOUND: NO MUSIC AT ALL, no score, no drums, no stings (music is added later). The soundtrack is only the spoken lines plus natural sound: engines, tyres, crowd, radio texture, room tone.
VOICES: Dana, @audio1. Theo, @audio2. Marcus, @audio3. TV commentator: American male, big broadcast baritone, fast and excited, a live broadcast feed. Spotter: American male, clipped tenor on the team radio. Journalist A: American woman, bright and eager.
PHYSICS: every object keeps one consistent physical state within a shot; phones and helmets never flip, morph or change shape; no flashes or glitch frames.
0 to 3 s: pit stop: wheel guns shriek, sparks, the crew swarms; Marcus leans into the cockpit with a tablet and says low and conspiratorial, a grin: "WhatsApp. Ten percent off. She'll bite."
3 to 11 s: the PushOwl Racing car blasts out of the pits and hunts the orange Ember Racing car, then dives down the inside and overtakes. The TV commentator, excited: "Vance out of the pits, right on Castell's gearbox!" One and a half seconds of pure engine roar. The spotter, sharp: "Inside's open. Go!" Theo on the radio, half a whisper: "Come on, Brenda." Dana on the radio, breaking into joy: "She bought them! Order's in!"
11 to 13.5 s: the chequered flag waves at the gantry as the PushOwl Racing car flashes under it, fireworks. The TV commentator, roaring: "Theo Vance wins the Port Aurelia Night Race!"
13.5 to 16.5 s: cockpit view on the slow-down lap, Theo punches the air. Dana on the radio, warm relief, a playful beat before the last words: "Congrats, Theo. You won the race. And the order."
16.5 to 18 s: podium: Theo sprays champagne, then sniffs the bottle like a candle, grinning.
18 to 20 s: the press conference room, camera flashes; Journalist A, bright and eager: "Theo, what's your secret?"
DELIVERY: every quoted line is spoken clearly, exactly as written, once, acted not read, the noted emotion in the face (on camera) and voice, natural breaths, stressed words stressed. Radio lines are clear and lightly compressed, never muffled. Nothing outside the quotes is ever spoken.
